recipes.title: Sri Lankan Parippu (Red Lentil Curry)
recipes.description: Creamy Sri Lankan red-lentil curry softened with light coconut milk and finished with a crackling coconut-oil tempering.

steps.title: Simmer the lentils
steps.text: Put the rinsed lentils in a saucepan with the water, half the onion, the green chillies, turmeric and curry powder. Simmer for 15 minutes until the lentils are soft and breaking down.
steps.visual: A steel saucepan of orange-yellow red lentils simmering with sliced onion and slit green chillies, steam rising

steps.title: Add coconut milk
steps.text: Stir in the light coconut milk and salt and simmer gently for 5 minutes until creamy. Don't let it boil hard.
steps.visual: Creamy pale-yellow dal in the same steel saucepan with a swirl of light coconut milk being stirred in

steps.title: Make the tempering
steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a small pan. Add mustard seeds, curry leaves, dried chilli, garlic and the remaining onion, and fry until the onion turns golden.
steps.visual: A small tadka pan with crackling mustard seeds, curry leaves, a dried red chilli, garlic slices and golden onion in coconut oil

steps.title: Temper and serve
steps.text: Pour the sizzling tempering over the dal. Serve with a big portion of cabbage mallung or greens instead of a second helping of rice.
steps.visual: Parippu in a clay bowl topped with the golden tempering of curry leaves and red chilli, a side of shredded green cabbage mallung

substitutions.note: Toned milk gives a similar creaminess if you don't have coconut milk.
Sambar powder works in a pinch; the flavour is less roasted.

recipes.storage: Refrigerate up to 3 days; it thickens as it cools.
recipes.reheating: Loosen with a splash of water and warm gently.

recipes.title: Light Sri Lankan Chicken Curry
recipes.description: Aromatic Sri Lankan chicken curry with roasted curry powder, cinnamon, cardamom and lemongrass, finished with a little light coconut milk.

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Rub the chicken with the curry powder, chilli powder, turmeric and salt. Leave for 15 minutes.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces in a steel bowl coated in dark roasted curry powder and red chilli

steps.title: Fry the whole spices
steps.text: Heat the oil and fry the cinnamon, cardamom, curry leaves, lemongrass and pandan for 30 seconds until fragrant.
steps.visual: A cinnamon stick, cardamom pods, curry leaves and a bruised lemongrass stalk sizzling in oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Soften the aromatics
steps.text: Add the onion, garlic and ginger and cook for about 4 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: Softened onion with garlic and ginger among the whole spices in the same kadai

steps.title: Cook the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and tomato, stir well, cover and cook for 20 minutes, stirring once or twice.
steps.visual: Spiced chicken pieces with tomato cooking under a lid in the kadai, juices bubbling

steps.title: Finish with coconut milk
steps.text: Stir in the light coconut milk and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes until the gravy coats the chicken.
steps.visual: Rich brown chicken curry with a lighter coconut gravy in the kadai, lemongrass visible

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Remove the whole spices and lemongrass and serve with a small portion of red rice and plenty of greens.
steps.visual: Sri Lankan chicken curry in a clay bowl with curry leaves, beside a small mound of red rice and a green salad

substitutions.note: Boneless thigh cooks faster — reduce the covered time to 12 minutes.
Whisked curd stirred in off the heat keeps it lighter still.

recipes.storage: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; the flavour deepens overnight.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently with a splash of water.

recipes.title: Lighter Chicken Karahi
recipes.description: Pakistani-style chicken karahi cooked down with fresh tomatoes, crushed whole spices and green chillies — 1 tbsp of oil instead of the restaurant half-cup.

ingredients.prep: 15 g crushed to a paste, 5 g julienned

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Heat the oil in a karahi or wok and sear the chicken on high heat for 5 minutes, turning, until it colours.
steps.visual: Chicken pieces searing and browning in a little oil in a black karahi over high flame

steps.title: Add ginger and garlic
steps.text: Add the ginger and garlic pastes and cook for 2 minutes. Keep the julienned ginger aside for the end.
steps.visual: Seared chicken coated in ginger and garlic paste in the same karahi

steps.title: Cook down the tomatoes
steps.text: Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and cook for 10 minutes until the tomatoes break down completely.
steps.visual: Chopped tomatoes collapsing into a thick red sauce around the chicken in the karahi, lid half off

steps.title: Spice and reduce
steps.text: Uncover, add the crushed cumin, coriander, black pepper, chilli flakes and green chillies, and cook on high until the sauce clings to the chicken.
steps.visual: Thick glossy tomato masala clinging to the chicken, flecked with crushed spices and slit green chillies

steps.title: Stir in the yoghurt
steps.text: Lower the heat, stir in the whisked curd and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.visual: Creamy orange-red karahi gravy after the yoghurt is stirred in

steps.title: Garnish and serve
steps.text: Top with the julienned ginger and coriander. Serve straight from the karahi with a salad and one small roti.
steps.visual: Chicken karahi in the karahi, topped with ginger matchsticks, fresh coriander and green chillies

substitutions.note: Hung curd adds a little more protein and won't split.
For mutton karahi, cook covered for 40 minutes after adding the tomatoes.

recipes.reheating: Reheat in a pan until bubbling.

recipes.title: Steamed Chicken Momos with Tomato Achar
recipes.description: Nepali steamed dumplings with a lean chicken-and-cabbage filling and a smoky roasted-tomato and sesame achar. One serving is about 8 momos.

steps.title: Knead the dough
steps.text: Mix the flour, a pinch of salt and the water into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest for 20 minutes.
steps.visual: A smooth ball of whole-wheat dough in a steel mixing bowl, covered with a damp cloth

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Combine the chicken mince, cabbage, onion, spring onion, ginger-garlic paste, soy sauce, pepper and salt and mix well with your hand.
steps.visual: Raw chicken mince mixed with finely chopped cabbage, onion and spring onion in a second steel bowl

steps.title: Fill and pleat
steps.text: Roll small, thin circles of dough, put a tablespoon of filling in each and pleat the edges closed. You'll get about 24 momos.
steps.visual: Neatly pleated raw momos lined up on a floured board next to thin dough circles and the bowl of filling

steps.title: Steam the momos
steps.text: Arrange the momos in a greased steamer without touching and steam for 12 to 15 minutes until the filling is cooked through.
steps.visual: Momos sitting in a steel steamer tray with steam rising, the dough now glossy and slightly translucent

steps.title: Blend the achar
steps.text: Roast the tomatoes over an open flame or in a dry pan until charred, then blend with the dried chillies, garlic, roasted sesame, lemon juice and salt until smooth.
steps.visual: Charred roasted tomatoes and toasted sesame seeds in a mixer jar beside a bowl of smooth orange-red achar

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve about 8 momos per person with the tomato achar and a crunchy cabbage-carrot salad.
steps.visual: Eight steamed momos on a plate with a small bowl of tomato-sesame achar and a cabbage-carrot salad

substitutions.note: Crumbled firm tofu with extra cabbage makes a vegetarian filling.
A rice-flour dough is gluten-free but tears more easily — roll thicker.

recipes.storage: Freeze uncooked momos on a tray, then bag them; steam from frozen for 18 minutes.

recipes.title: Nepali Dal Bhat Tarkari Bowl
recipes.description: Nepal's everyday plate made lighter: a modest scoop of brown rice with a generous bowl of black-lentil dal and potato–cauliflower tarkari.

steps.title: Cook the brown rice
steps.text: Cook the brown rice in about 1½ cups of water until tender, about 25 minutes (or 3 whistles in a pressure cooker).
steps.visual: Brown rice simmering in a steel saucepan with small steam holes on the surface

steps.title: Pressure-cook the dal
steps.text: Pressure-cook the lentils with turmeric, salt and the remaining water for 5 to 6 whistles until soft, then mash lightly.
steps.visual: Soft, dark black-lentil dal in an open pressure cooker being mashed with a ladle

steps.title: Temper the dal
steps.text: Heat the ghee, add cumin (or jimbu) and garlic until golden, and pour over the dal.
steps.visual: Golden garlic and cumin sizzling in ghee being poured over the dark dal

steps.title: Cook the tarkari
steps.text: Crackle the fenugreek in oil, add the potato, cauliflower, peas, tomato and cumin powder with salt and a splash of water. Cover and cook for 12 minutes until tender.
steps.visual: Potato cubes, cauliflower florets and green peas cooking with tomato in a kadai

steps.title: Build the bowl
steps.text: Serve a small mound of rice with a generous bowl of dal and tarkari, and cucumber on the side.
steps.visual: A Nepali thali-style bowl with a small scoop of brown rice, a large bowl of black dal, potato-cauliflower tarkari and sliced cucumber

substitutions.note: Whole moong cooks faster (3 whistles) and is lighter on the stomach.
Foxtail millet gives more fibre per bite.

recipes.storage: Store components separately for up to 3 days.
recipes.reheating: Warm dal and tarkari separately; sprinkle rice with water before reheating.

recipes.title: Goan Prawn Chilli Fry
recipes.description: A quick Goan stir-fry of prawns tossed with onion, capsicum and tomato in a tangy Kashmiri-chilli and vinegar masala.

steps.title: Marinate the prawns
steps.text: Toss the prawns with the Kashmiri chilli, turmeric, cumin, vinegar and salt and leave for 10 minutes.
steps.visual: Peeled prawns coated in bright red chilli marinade in a steel bowl

steps.title: Sauté the aromatics
steps.text: Heat the oil and sauté the garlic, ginger and onion for 3 minutes until the onion softens.
steps.visual: Sliced onion with garlic and ginger softening in a little oil in a black kadai

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Add the capsicum and tomato and cook for 2 minutes so they stay slightly crisp.
steps.visual: Green capsicum strips and tomato tossed with the onions in the same kadai

steps.title: Stir-fry the prawns
steps.text: Add the prawns and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes until just pink and curled. Don't overcook or they turn rubbery.
steps.visual: Pink, curled prawns glazed in red masala with capsicum and onion in the kadai

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Finish with coriander and serve with a salad, or one small pao for a fuller meal.
steps.visual: Goan prawn chilli fry on a white plate scattered with coriander, a lime wedge and a fresh salad beside it

substitutions.note: Squid rings work the same way — cook for just 2 minutes.
Lemon juice gives a fresher sourness if you don't have toddy or coconut vinegar.

recipes.storage: Best eaten fresh; refrigerate up to 1 day.
recipes.reheating: Warm briefly in a hot pan.

recipes.title: Soya Chunk Vegetable Pulao
recipes.description: A one-pot vegetable pulao bulked up with soya chunks for 20+ g of plant protein per plate, fragrant with whole spices and mint.

steps.title: Prepare the soya
steps.text: Boil the soya chunks in plenty of water for 5 minutes, drain, squeeze out the water and halve them.
steps.visual: Plump boiled soya chunks squeezed dry and halved on a plate beside a strainer

steps.title: Fry the spices and onion
steps.text: Heat the oil with the bay leaf, cloves, cardamom and cumin, then add the onion and cook until golden.
steps.visual: Golden sliced onion with whole spices sizzling in an open pressure cooker

steps.title: Add soya and vegetables
steps.text: Add the ginger-garlic paste, then the carrot, beans, peas, capsicum and soya. Cook for 3 minutes.
steps.visual: Colourful diced vegetables and soya chunks tossed with the onions in the pressure cooker

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Add the drained rice, garam masala, salt and water. Cover and cook on low for 12 to 15 minutes, or 2 whistles in a pressure cooker.
steps.visual: Rice grains and vegetables submerged in water in the pressure cooker just before closing the lid

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Let it rest for 5 minutes, fluff with a fork, fold in the mint and serve with cucumber raita.
steps.visual: Fluffy soya vegetable pulao on a plate with mint leaves, a bowl of cucumber raita alongside

substitutions.note: Brown rice needs 3 whistles and ½ cup more water.
Paneer cubes, added at the end, if you prefer dairy protein.

recipes.reheating: Sprinkle with water and microwave covered, or steam.

recipes.title: Sri Lankan Ambul Thiyal (Sour Tuna Curry)
recipes.description: Southern Sri Lanka's dry, sour fish curry — tuna cooked slowly in a goraka, pepper and chilli paste until almost dry. Very lean and keeps well.

steps.title: Soak the goraka
steps.text: Soak the goraka in a little hot water for 10 minutes until soft.
steps.visual: Dark pieces of dried goraka softening in a small bowl of hot water

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Grind the soaked goraka with the garlic, ginger, black pepper and chilli powder into a thick paste.
steps.visual: A thick dark-red goraka and pepper paste in an open mixer jar

steps.title: Coat the fish
steps.text: Coat the tuna cubes in the paste with turmeric and salt.
steps.visual: Cubes of deep-red tuna evenly coated in the dark spice paste in a steel bowl

steps.title: Layer the pot
steps.text: Line a clay or heavy pot with curry leaves, pandan and cinnamon, add the fish in one layer and pour in the water.
steps.visual: Coated tuna cubes sitting on a bed of curry leaves, pandan and a cinnamon stick in a clay pot with a little water

steps.title: Cook until almost dry
steps.text: Cook on low for 20 to 25 minutes, turning the pieces gently, until the liquid has almost gone and the fish is coated.
steps.visual: Dark, glossy, almost-dry tuna pieces in the clay pot, the sauce reduced to a sticky coating

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Drizzle with the coconut oil and rest. The flavour improves the next day — cook a batch for lunches and serve with red rice and greens.
steps.visual: Ambul thiyal in the clay pot with a sheen of coconut oil, served with red rice and a green mallung

substitutions.note: Seer fish (neymeen) holds its shape well in this slow-cooked curry.
Use 2 tbsp tamarind paste if you can't find goraka; it's a little sweeter.

recipes.storage: Keeps 4 days refrigerated — traditionally made to last.
recipes.reheating: Warm gently, covered, with a spoonful of water.
